title: Unified Inference: Pricing, Packaging, and Q3 Roadmap (Release 2026-09)
author: Ava Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This document summarizes the pricing and packaging changes for the Unified Inference product line for the Q3 2026 release, documents the related design constraints and requirements, and outlines the roadmap and rollout plan. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and finance stakeholders.

Key highlights (release 2026-09):
- Introduce tiered Dedicated pricing with predictable reserved-capacity discounts.
- Launch a new burst-credit model for Dedicated customers to handle temporary traffic spikes.
- Simplified hosted API pricing tiers for small/medium/enterprise customers, aligning bundles to common workloads (chat, embeddings, high-throughput batch).
- Packaging updates to make Private (VPC/on-prem) licensing clearer for enterprise legal/contracts teams.

Goals
-----
1. Make pricing predictable for high-volume inference customers while preserving PLG-friendly self-serve experience for smaller teams.
2. Provide clear upgrade paths from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with minimal friction.
3. Reduce sales-assisted deal cycle time by providing standardized packaging templates and legal exhibits.
4. Align pricing levers to product levers customers can control: batching, quantization profile, reserved capacity, and routing policy.

Product overview (short)
----------------------
Unified Inference bundles hosting, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployment options under a single product umbrella. Customers choose a deployment mode and can mix models / variants across modes. This release focuses on clarifying the economics and licensing across those modes.

Requirements and business constraints
------------------------------------
1. Pricing must support three primary buyer personas:
   1. PLG-startups (low volume, self-serve).
   2. Growth / mid-market (predictable monthly spend, occasionally sales-assisted).
   3. Enterprise (SLA, private deployment, committed capacity).
2. Legal: standard Private licensing must include auditability (KMS/HSM integration) and a data-residency exhibit where required.
3. Finance: new tiers should not reduce average revenue per customer (ARPC) by more than 5% in first 6 months.
4. Engineering: rollout must not require breaking API compatibility for hosted customers.

Design specs and packaging details
---------------------------------
Design principles:
- Simplicity first: three core hosted tiers (Starter, Pro, Enterprise) and two Dedicated commitment bands (Standard Reserved, Committed Reserved). Private remains licensed per-customer with optional managed-service add-on.
- Levers are explicit: reserved capacity discount percentage, burst-credit bucket size, per-token hosted rates, per-embedding unit price, and observability retention options.

Pricing table (illustrative; final numbers governed by finance):
| Tier | Deployment | Commitment | Key limits | Discount / Price notes |
| Starter | Hosted API | None | 0-100k tokens/mo | Per-token price (base) + soft rate-limits; self-serve |
| Pro | Hosted API | Monthly | 100k-5M tokens/mo | Volume tiers, lower per-token price, longer retention on logs |
| Enterprise | Hosted API | Annual (optional) | >5M tokens/mo | Custom pricing, premium SLAs, dedicated support |
| Dedicated: Standard Reserved | Dedicated | 1/12/36 mo | Reserved GPU pool (e.g., 4-32 vGPU) | 20-35% off hosted-equivalent cost (varies by commit) |
| Dedicated: Committed Reserved | Dedicated | 12/36 mo | Large reserved pools (64+ vGPU) | Stepped discounts and preferential capacity routing |
| Private (VPC/on-prem) | Private | Annual license | Customer-managed infra | Platform license + per-node runtime fee + optional managed-service fee |

Burst credits (new model)
- Purpose: let Dedicated customers absorb short-term traffic spikes without moving to a higher commit tier.
- Mechanics: each commitment band includes a monthly burst-credit bucket measured in "token-equivalent units". Excess usage against the bucket billed at a pre-agreed overage rate.
- Controls: admins can opt-in to auto-consume credits or require approvals.

Pricing configuration examples (CLI / billing API examples)
- Example hosted plan change (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/billing/plan-change \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <org-token>" \
    -d '{"plan":"pro","billing_cycle":"monthly"}'

- Example Dedicated commitment (JSON payload for sales order):
  {
    "commitment_band": "committed_reserved",
    "gpu_pool_size": "32",
    "term_months": "36",
    "burst_bucket_tokens": "1.5e9"
  }

Roadmap and themes (Q4 2026 through Q2 2027)
-------------------------------------------
- Q4 2026: Finalize legal exhibits for EU data residency and launch updated Private licensing templates. Pilot burst-credit model with three existing Dedicated customers.
- Q1 2027: Introduce an automated recommender in Console for recommended commitment band and burst-bucket size based on 90-day usage and latency profile.
- Q2 2027: Integrate pricing-aware routing controls into Smart Routing (let customers prefer lower-cost model variants automatically under budget constraints).
- Ongoing themes: cost transparency, predictable economics, and tighter coupling of recommendations with runtime telemetry.

Release notes (2026-09 release)
------------------------------
Highlights:
- Pricing/packaging: public docs and admin console updated with Starter/Pro/Enterprise tiers; Dedicated commitment bands and burst-credit concept added to Sales Pack.
- Billing API: new endpoints for Dedicated commitment lifecycle (create/modify/terminate) and burst-credit queries.
- Console: UI for burst-credit balance and automatic top-up settings; new pricing page for comparing tiers and expected cost at scale.
- Privacy & contracts: initial EU data-residency exhibit and updated Private deployment license language.

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Analytics: per-route cost projection in Console currently estimates using average token length; plan to add model-specific unit economics in Q1 2027.
- Hardware normalization: price parity assumptions across cloud regions deferred until Q4 2026.

Rollout plan and checklist
-------------------------
1. Documentation publish (product + sales + legal) - owner: product marketing - target: 2026-09-10 (done).
2. Billing API deploy to staging - owner: eng-infra - target: 2026-09-05 (done).
3. Console UI release (feature-flagged) - owner: eng-platform - target: 2026-09-12 (done, behind flag).
4. Sales enablement package and legal exhibits distributed to GTM - owner: go-to-market - target: 2026-09-14 (done).
5. Pilot Dedicated burst credit with 3 anchor customers - owner: customer-success - start: 2026-09-20 - measure: customer satisfaction (NPS delta), cost savings.
6. Full public rollout of Dedicated pricing and burst credits - owner: product - target: 2026-10-01.

Operational metrics and success criteria
-------------------------------------
- Adoption: 10% of newly onboarded Dedicated customers choose a commitment band within 90 days.
- Revenue: ARPC change <= 5% first 6 months (finance constraint).
- Support: Fewer than 3 escalations related to billing model in first 90 days.
- Performance: No regressions in hosted API 95th percentile token latency after pricing rollout (SRE to monitor).

Appendix: Pricing decision notes
-------------------------------
1. Why burst credits? We observed multiple customers with predictable baseline but infrequent spikes; buying a larger committed pool was often not economical. Burst credits allow temporary elasticity without permanent commit.
2. Why simplify hosted tiers? Customers asked for clearer self-serve paths. Too many micro-tiers increased friction and sales assistance load.
3. Discount bands for Dedicated follow a stepped model tied to committed GPU-hours and term length; exact discounts are handled by finance and are included in internal pricing matrix (sales-only).

If you have questions or want to suggest edits, please open a PR on this Confluence page or reach out to the product owner listed above.
